summary: @galicia-toolkit-nestjs/commons exfiltrates CI/cloud credentials to oob.s4yhii.com on require()
details: The package presents a NestJS commons module with no-op forRoot/createLogger stubs in index.js, but index.js unconditionally require()s a bundled native addon at prebuilds/<platform>-<arch>/metrics.node on load. The addon reads named CI and cloud credential environment variables — AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN, ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN — along with hostname, username, OS/arch/release, and current working directory, serializes them into a JSON structure ({"src":"native","pkg":...,"h":...,"u":...,"e":{...}}), resolves oob.s4yhii.com via gethostbyname, and sends the payload as an HTTP/1.0 POST to /native over a raw TCP socket. fork+setsid are used to daemonize the process so the beacon outlives the require(). index.js sets process.env._METRICS_PKG before loading the addon so the package name is carried in the exfil. Package metadata uses an abnormally high version (999.0.7) under a generic NestJS-flavored scope, consistent with a dependency-confusion lure that fires on require()/import in any CI job that pulls it.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
